title: If Things Were Different
grammarNote: Present/future-unreal hypotheticals pair a 'si' clause in the imperfect subjunctive (si tuviera, si fuera, si pudiera) with a main clause in the conditional tense (haría, sería, podría, tendría) — 'si tuviera más tiempo, viajaría más'. Advice formulas like 'yo que tú', 'en tu lugar', and 'deberías' offer a softer, more formal way to suggest a course of action than a direct command. This lesson stays entirely in present/future-unreal territory; past-unreal hypotheticals are covered at a later level.

phrases.target: Si tuviera más tiempo, viajaría más
phrases.native: If I had more time, I would travel more
phrases.phonetic: see too-vee-EH-rah mahs TYEM-poh, bee-ah-hah-REE-ah mahs
phrases.vocabularyIntro: This is the classic present-unreal hypothetical pattern: 'si' + imperfect subjunctive (tuviera) + conditional (viajaría) for a situation that isn't currently true.

exampleSentence.target: Si tuviera más tiempo libre, viajaría más seguido.
exampleSentence.native: If I had more free time, I would travel more often.

phrases.grammarNote: 'Tuviera' is the imperfect subjunctive of 'tener'; the conditional 'viajaría' comes from the infinitive 'viajar' plus the ending '-ía'.
phrases.memoryHook: Picture yourself with a suitcase you never use — 'si tuviera tiempo' is the wish, 'viajaría' is the dream trip.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: If I had more time, I would travel more
practiceItems.answer: Si tuviera más tiempo, viajaría más

practiceItems.prompt: ¿Qué harías si tuvieras más tiempo libre?
practiceItems.answer: Si tuviera más tiempo, viajaría más

phrases.target: Yo que tú, hablaría con tu jefe
phrases.native: If I were you, I would talk to your boss
phrases.phonetic: yoh keh too, ah-blah-REE-ah kon too HEH-feh
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Yo que tú' (literally 'I that you') is a fixed advice formula meaning 'if I were you', always followed by the conditional tense.

exampleSentence.target: Yo que tú, hablaría con tu jefe antes de decidir.
exampleSentence.native: If I were you, I would talk to your boss before deciding.

phrases.grammarNote: 'Yo que tú' never changes form regardless of who is being advised; only the verb after it shifts into the conditional.
phrases.memoryHook: Think of stepping into someone's shoes: 'yo que tú' swaps your identity for theirs before giving advice.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: If I were you, I would talk to your boss
practiceItems.answer: Yo que tú, hablaría con tu jefe

practiceItems.prompt: Yo que tú, ___ con tu jefe.
¿Qué me recomiendas hacer con mi jefe?
practiceItems.answer: Yo que tú, hablaría con tu jefe

phrases.target: En tu lugar, no aceptaría esa oferta
phrases.native: In your place, I wouldn't accept that offer
phrases.phonetic: en too loo-GAR, no ah-sep-tah-REE-ah EH-sah oh-FEHR-tah
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'En tu lugar' (in your place/shoes) works exactly like 'yo que tú' as a softer alternative for giving advice.

exampleSentence.target: En tu lugar, no aceptaría esa oferta de trabajo.
exampleSentence.native: In your place, I wouldn't accept that job offer.

phrases.grammarNote: 'Aceptaría' is the regular conditional of 'aceptar', formed by adding '-ía' to the infinitive.
phrases.memoryHook: 'Lugar' means 'place' — imagine literally standing in the other person's place before giving your honest advice.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: In your place, I wouldn't accept that offer
practiceItems.answer: En tu lugar, no aceptaría esa oferta

practiceItems.prompt: En tu lugar, no ___ esa oferta.

practiceItems.answer: En tu lugar, no aceptaría esa oferta

phrases.target: Si fuera tú, me mudaría a otra ciudad
phrases.native: If I were you, I would move to another city
phrases.phonetic: see FWEH-rah too, meh moo-dah-REE-ah ah OH-trah see-oo-DAHD
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Si fuera tú' is a fuller, more explicit version of 'yo que tú' using the imperfect subjunctive of 'ser' (fuera).

exampleSentence.target: Si fuera tú, me mudaría a otra ciudad este año.
exampleSentence.native: If I were you, I would move to another city this year.

phrases.grammarNote: 'Fuera' is the irregular imperfect subjunctive of 'ser'; note it looks identical to the imperfect subjunctive of 'ir'.
phrases.memoryHook: 'Fuera' sounds like 'afuera' (outside) — imagine stepping outside your own life into someone else's to give advice.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: If I were you, I would move to another city
practiceItems.answer: Si fuera tú, me mudaría a otra ciudad

practiceItems.prompt: Si ___ tú, me mudaría a otra ciudad.
¿Qué harías tú en mi lugar con la mudanza?
practiceItems.answer: Si fuera tú, me mudaría a otra ciudad
